title: Do Not Build Fortresses to Protect Yourself - Isolation Is Dangerous
coreMove: Stay in circulation so information and adjustment reach you before danger hardens
sourcePressure: Chapter 18 is supported here by the frozen title and grouped secondary summaries: isolation can feel protective but often increases danger because it cuts a person off from information, contact, movement, and adjustment. The mechanism should stay narrow. The chapter is about fortress thinking, stale assumptions, and the cost of defensive withdrawal, not about condemning all privacy or all boundaries. Keep it grounded in information loss, circulation, selective contact, and the limit that openness still requires judgment. Avoid invented court, palace, or battlefield anecdotes and avoid turning the law into generic networking advice. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
